Presidential Documents
60793 Federal Register / Vol. 80, No. 194 / Wednesday, October 7, 2015 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 13709 of October 2, 2015 
National Security Medal 
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States 
and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces of the United States, 
it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Policy. In order to more appropriately recognize distinguished 
achievements and outstanding contributions in the field of national security, 
Executive Order 10431 of January 19, 1953, is amended as follows: 
(a) Section 2 is amended to read as follows: ‘‘The National Security 
Medal may be awarded to any person, without regard to nationality, including 
members of the Armed Forces of the United States, for distinguished achieve-
ment or outstanding contribution made on or after July 26, 1947, in the 
field of national security through either exceptionally meritorious service 
performed in a position of high responsibility or through an act of heroism 
requiring personal courage of a high degree and complete disregard of per-
sonal safety.’’; and 
(b) By inserting at the end: 
‘‘7. Any individual having personal knowledge of the facts of a potential 
recipient’s exceptionally meritorious service or act of heroism, either as 
an eyewitness or from the testimony of others who have personal knowledge 
or were eyewitnesses, may recommend the potential recipient as a candidate 
for the award to the Executive Secretary of the National Security Council. 
Any recommendations shall be made with the concurrence of the department 
or agency employing the proposed recipient, if appropriate, and be accom-
panied by complete documentation, including, where necessary, certificates, 
affidavits, or sworn transcripts of testimony. Each recommendation for an 
award shall show the exact status, at the time of the rendition of the 
service on which the recommendation is based, with respect to citizenship, 
employment, and all other material factors of the person who is being 
recommended for the National Security Medal. Each recommendation shall 
contain a draft of an appropriate citation to accompany the award of the 
National Security Medal. 
‘‘8. Upon a determination by the Executive Secretary of the National 
Security Council that the National Security Medal is warranted, and following 
approval by the President, the Executive Secretary shall notify the Office 
of the Director of National Intelligence, which will then process the award 
recommendation, prepare the National Security Medal, with any appropriate 
devices, and deliver the National Security Medal to the National Security 
Council for presentation to the recipient.’’ 
Sec. 2. This order supersedes the regulations governing the award of the 
National Security Medal issued with Presidential approval on January 19, 
1953, and published with Executive Order 10431. 
Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department, agency, or 
the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

research_rationale:
EO 13709 (Obama, signed 2015-10-02, 80 FR 60793, published 2015-10-07) amends Executive Order 10431 of January 19, 1953 (National Security Medal): section 1(a) restates section 2 of EO 10431 to say who may be awarded the medal, section 1(b) adds paragraphs 7 and 8 on recommendations and processing, section 2 supersedes the regulations governing the award issued with Presidential approval on January 19, 1953, and section 3 states general provisions (no impairment of agency authority or OMB functions, implementation consistent with law and appropriations, no private right). The dossier inventory held only the first sentence of section 1 (characters 859-1011), so the inventory is corrected with overrides to seven scopes covering the whole text from the policy sentence through section 3(c). The text sets no term or condition. The held U.S. Code prints EO 10431 as amended by section 1 of EO 13709, which shows the amendments are part of the current text, and prints a note on section 2; neither the Code, the eCFR search nor the Federal Register disposition notes show any later amendment or revocation. The order cites no statute as authority (President and Commander in Chief), so no authority statute needs checking. Section 2 is a one-time supersession that took effect on signing, since the order states no other effective date, and is recorded as exhausted by performance; its surviving consequence (the 1953 regulations remain superseded) is separate.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: sections 1 and 3 state no term or condition, and no held later order revokes or amends EO 13709 or restates EO 10431 again. Section 2 is ended only in the sense that its one-time supersession was performed on signing, 2015-10-02.","independent_command_check":"The amendments in section 1 and the supersession in section 2 are independent: the amendments continue in the text of EO 10431 while the supersession was a one-time act. The general provisions are rules of construction that continue.","savings_check":"The only savings question is the status of the superseded 1953 regulations, which the Code note records as superseded; no residual command exists.","scope_check":"Seven scopes: the policy sentence introducing the amendments, section 1(a) (restated section 2 of EO 10431), section 1(b) (new paragraphs 7 and 8), section 2 (supersession of the 1953 regulations), and section 3(a), 3(b) and 3(c) (general provisions). Under the owner strike-and-insert ruling the amendments continue as part of the amended order."}

savings_residuals.reason: The amendments to EO 10431 stand as part of that order's current text and no later instrument ends them; the superseded 1953 regulations stay superseded. Nothing else remains to save.

6370
Federal Register 
Vol. 51, No, 35
Presidential Documents
Friday February 21, 1908
Title 3— Executive Order 12549 of February 18, 1986
T he Presid en t D ebarm ent and Suspension
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, and in order to curb fraud, waste, and abuse in 
Federal programs, increase agency accountability, and ensure consistency 
among agency regulations concerning debarment and suspension of partici­
pants in Federal programs, it is hereby ordered that:
Section 1. (a) To the extent permitted by law and subject to the limitations in 
Section 1(c), Executive departments and agencies shall participate in a 
system for debarment and suspension from programs and activities involving 
Federal financial and nonfinancial assistance and benefits. Debarment or 
suspension of a participant in a program by one agency shall have govern­
ment-wide effect.
(b) Activities covered by this Order include but are not limited to: grants, 
cooperative agreements, contracts of assistance, loans, and loan guarantees.
(c) This Order does not cover procurement programs and activities, direct 
Federal statutory entitlements or mandatory awards, direct awards to foreign 
governments or public international organizations, benefits to an individual as 
a personal entitlement, or Federal employment.
Sec. 2. To the extent permitted by law, Executive departments and agencies 
shall:
(a) Follow government-wide criteria and government-wide minimum due proc­
ess procedures when they act to debar or suspend participants in affected 
programs.
(b) Send to the agency designated pursuant to Section 5 identifying informa­
tion concerning debarred and suspended participants in affected programs, 
participants who have agreed to exclusion from participation, and participants 
declared ineligible under applicable law, including Executive Orders. This 
information shall be included in the list to be maintained pursuant to 
Section 5.
(c) Not allow a party to participate in any affected program if any Executive 
department or agency has debarred, suspended, or otherwise excluded (to the 
extent specified in the exclusion agreement) that party from participation in 
an affected program. An agency may grant an exception permitting a de­
barred, suspended, or excluded party to participate in a particular transaction 
upon a written determination by the agency head or authorized designee 
stating the reason(s) for deviating from this Presidential policy. However, I 
intend that exceptions to this policy should be granted only infrequently.
Sec. 3. Executive departments and agencies shall issue regulations governing 
their implementation of this Order that shall be consistent with the guidelines 
issued under Section 6. Proposed regulations shall be submitted to the Office 
of Management and Budget for review within four months of the date of the 
guidelines issued under Section 6. The Director of the Office of Management 
and Budget may return for reconsideration proposed regulations that the 
Director believes are inconsistent with the guidelines. Final regulations shall 
be published within twelve months of the date of the guidelines.
Sec. 4. There is hereby constituted the Interagency Committee on Debarment 
and Suspension, which shall monitor implementation of this Order. The

=== PDF page 167 of 192 ===
Federal Register /  Vol. 51, No. 35 /  Friday, February 21, 1986 /  Presidential Documents 6371
Committee shall consist of representatives of agencies designated by the 
Director of the Office of Management and Budget.
Sec. 5. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall designate a 
Federal agency to perform the following functions: maintain a current list of 
all individuals and organizations excluded from program participation under 
this Order, periodically distribute the list to Federal agencies, and study the 
feasibility of automating the list; coordinate with the lead agency responsible 
for government-wide debarment and suspension of contractors; chair the 
Interagency Committee established by Section 4; and report periodically to the 
Director on implementation of this Order, with the first report due within two 
years of the date of the Order.
Sec. 6. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget is authorized to 
issue guidelines to Executive departments and agencies that govern which 
programs and activities are covered by this Order, prescribe government-wide 
criteria and government-wide minimum due process procedures, and set forth 
other related details for the effective administration of the guidelines.
Sec. 7. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall report to 
the President within three years of the date of this Order on Federal agency 
compliance with the Order, including the number of exceptions made under 
Section 2(c), and shall make such recommendations as are appropriate further 
to curb fraud, waste, and abuse.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
F e b r u a r y  18, 1986.
[FR Doc. 86-3897  
Filed 2-19-86; 10:56 am]  
Billing code 3195-01-M

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, and in order to curb fraud, waste, and abuse in

among agency regulations concerning debarment and suspension of partici­
pants in Federal programs, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1(c), Executive departments and agencies shall participate in a 
system for debarment and suspension from programs and activities involving

suspension of a participant in a program by one agency shall have govern­
ment-wide effect.

cooperative agreements, contracts of assistance, loans, and loan guarantees.

Federal statutory entitlements or mandatory awards, direct awards to foreign 
governments or public international organizations, benefits to an individual as 
a personal entitlement, or Federal employment.

shall:
(a) Follow government-wide criteria and government-wide minimum due proc­
ess procedures when they act to debar or suspend participants in affected 
programs.

participants who have agreed to exclusion from participation, and participants

department or agency has debarred, suspended, or otherwise excluded (to the 
extent specified in the exclusion agreement) that party from participation in 
an affected program. An agency may grant an exception permitting a de­
barred, suspended, or excluded party to participate in a particular transaction 
upon a written determination by the agency head or authorized designee 
stating the reason(s) for deviating from this Presidential policy. However, I 
intend that exceptions to this policy should be granted only infrequently.

their implementation of this Order that shall be consistent with the guidelines

and Suspension, which shall monitor implementation of this Order. The

research_rationale:
EO 12549 (Reagan, signed 1986-02-18, 51 FR 6370, published 1986-02-21) establishes a government-wide system of debarment and suspension for nonprocurement programs: executive departments and agencies shall participate in the system and a debarment or suspension by one agency has government-wide effect (section 1(a)), the activities covered (section 1(b)) and the programs not covered, including procurement (section 1(c)); agencies shall follow government-wide criteria and minimum due process procedures (section 2(a)), report debarred and suspended participants (section 2(b)) and not allow a party excluded by any agency to participate except by written exception (section 2(c)); agencies shall issue implementing regulations consistent with OMB guidelines, with deadlines of four and twelve months from the guidelines (section 3); the Interagency Committee on Debarment and Suspension is constituted (section 4); OMB designates an agency to keep the exclusion list and chair the committee, with a first report due within two years (section 5); OMB may issue guidelines (section 6); and OMB reports to the President within three years (section 7). The dossier inventory numbered the clauses incorrectly (the section 2(c) text was labelled section 5, and section 3 and parts of sections 5 to 7 were mislabelled or merged), so the inventory is corrected with overrides to twelve scopes, one per paragraph or section, covering every operative part of the held text after the preamble. The held current sources show the order in effect: a note in the U.S. Code under 31 U.S.C. 6101 prints it and a statute enacted in 2008 and amended in 2011 and 2013 identifies the committee by reference to sections 4 and 5 of the order, and 2 CFR 180.110 in the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 still refers to exclusions under the order. EO 12689 (1989), which the Federal Register note lists as a cross-reference, extends government-wide effect of debarment to procurement and expressly refers to nonprocurement activities covered by EO 12549; it recites EO 12549 and does not amend or revoke it. EO 13904 (2020) also only recites EO 12549 as policy. The order cites no statute as authority (the Constitution and laws of the United States), so no authority statute needs checking. The deadlines in sections 3, 5 and 7 are deadlines, not ends; no held source dates performance of those one-time steps, so no end is recorded for them.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: no section states a term or condition, and the later orders that name EO 12549 (EO 12689 and EO 13904) only recite or build on it; no held source shows a later general rule extinguishing any command in it. Deadlines in sections 3, 5 and 7 are not ends.","independent_command_check":"The participation duty, the covered-activities and exclusions text, the three duties in section 2, the regulation-issuing duty, the committee, the list and designation duty, the guidelines authority and the reporting duty are independent; none depends on another for its continuation.","savings_check":"No ending event, so no savings question arises; regulations issued under section 3 and guidelines under section 6 continue to stand in the CFR.","scope_check":"Twelve scopes: sections 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 2(a), 2(b), 2(c), 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. Section 2 is split because its lead-in and paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) command different things. The preamble states purposes and commands nothing."}

Tuesday, December 3, 1963 FEDERAL REGISTER 12787
v  Executive Order 11129
DESIGNATING CERTAIN FACILITIES OF THE NATIONAL AERONAUTICS
AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION AND OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DE­
FENSE, IN THE STATE OF FLORIDA, AS THE JOHN F. KENNEDY
SPACE CENTER
W HEREAS President John F. Kennedy lighted the imagination  
of our people when he set the moon as our -target and man as the  
means to reach it ;  and
W HEREAS the installations now to be renamed are a center and  
symbol of our country’s peaceful assault on space; and
W HEREAS it is in the nature of this assault that it should test  
the limits of our youth and grace, our strength and wit, our vigor  
and perseverance—qualities fitting to the memory of John F. Kennedy:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me as  
President of the United States, I hereby designate the facilities of  
the Launch Operations Center of the National Aeronautics and Space  
Administration and the facilities of Station No. 1 of the Atlantic  
Missile Range, in the State of Florida, as the John F. Kennedy Space  
Center; and such facilities shall be hereafter known and referred to  
by that name.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
T h e W hite  H ouse,
November 29,1963.
[F.R. Doc. 63-12542; Filed, Nov. 29,1963 :  4 :13 p.m.]

research_rationale:
EO 11129 (Johnson, signed 1963-11-29, 28 FR 12787, Federal Register of 1963-12-03) designates the facilities of the Launch Operations Center of NASA and of Station No. 1 of the Atlantic Missile Range in Florida as the John F. Kennedy Space Center and directs that they be known by that name. The held text is a single sentence with no expiry or condition. The Federal Register disposition notes name no amendment or revocation. The current U.S. Code, 51 U.S.C. 20306(a)(6)(B) (added by Pub. L. 119-21, title IV, section 40005(a), July 4, 2025), refers to the center described in Executive Order 11129 (28 Fed. Reg. 12787), which shows the designation is treated as in effect. The order cites no statute as authority (it relies on the President's constitutional authority), so no authority statute needs checking.

research_rationale:
EO 10860 (Eisenhower, signed 1960-02-05, 25 FR 1089, published 1960-02-09) prescribes the design of the Coat of Arms of the President (section 1), the Seal of the President (section 2), the Color and Flag of the President (section 3), makes the designs, as shown in the accompanying illustrations and specifications, exclusive to the President (section 4), and provides that it becomes effective on July 4, 1960 when it supersedes EO 10823 of May 26, 1959 (section 5). The dossier inventory ran sections 2 and 3 together because the OCR prints the section 3 marker with a doubled period, so the inventory is corrected with overrides to five scopes covering every section of the held text. The text has no expiry or condition, and a search of the held corpus for the order number finds only its own text and the 1989 codification. The Federal Register disposition note records only that it supersedes EO 10823. The U.S. Code and eCFR bounded searches found no hit, and the machine searches record no amendment or revocation, so the claim rests on the held original plus those bounded searches; this is a negative-search predicate, and the accompanying illustrations and specifications are not held.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: sections 1 to 4 state no term or condition, section 5 only fixes the effective date of July 4, 1960 (long past) and supersedes EO 10823, and no held instrument revokes or replaces EO 10860.","independent_command_check":"The design prescriptions in sections 1 to 3 and the exclusivity command in section 4 are independent standing commands; the supersession of EO 10823 in section 5 is a separate one-time effect that stays in place because EO 10823 has been replaced, not revived.","savings_check":"No savings clause and no ending event, so no residual question arises; the supersession of EO 10823 is complete.","scope_check":"Five scopes: section 1 (Coat of Arms), section 2 (Seal), section 3 (Color and Flag), section 4 (designs as described and illustrated, exclusive use) and section 5 (effective date and supersession of EO 10823). Each is treated separately; none depends on the order ending in part."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order is a standing prescription of designs with no end; the only transition it effects (superseding EO 10823 on July 4, 1960) is already complete, and no later instrument ending or amending the order was found in the bounded searches, so there is no residual to save.

Executive Order 12568 of October 2, 1986
Employment Opportunities for Military Spouses at Nonappro-  
priated Fund A ctivities
By the authority vested in me as President by the laws of the United States of  
America, including section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, it is  
ordered that the Secretary of Defense and, as designated by him for this  
purpose, any of the Secretaries, Under Secretaries, and Assistant Secretaries  
of the Military Departments, are hereby empowered to exercise the discretion­
ary authority granted to the President by subsection 806(a)(2) of the Depart­
ment of Defense Authorization Act of 1986, Public Law No. 99-145, to give  
preference in hiring for positions in nonappropriated fund activities to quali­
fied spouses of members of the Armed Forces stationed in the same geographi­
cal area as the nonappropriated fund activity for positions in wage grade UA-  
8 and below and equivalent positions and for positions paid at hourly rates.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
O c to b e r 2, 1986.

research_rationale:
EO 12568 (Reagan, signed 1986-10-02, 51 FR 35497, published 1986-10-06) empowers the Secretary of Defense and, as designated by him, the Secretaries, Under Secretaries and Assistant Secretaries of the Military Departments to exercise the discretionary authority granted to the President by subsection 806(a)(2) of the Department of Defense Authorization Act of 1986 (Public Law 99-145) to give hiring preference in nonappropriated fund activities to qualified spouses of members of the Armed Forces stationed in the same area, for positions in wage grade UA-8 and below, equivalent positions and positions paid at hourly rates. The authority statute was replaced rather than repealed: section 568(d) of Pub. L. 104-106 (February 10, 1996), printed in the held U.S. Code notes to 10 U.S.C. 1784, provides that the order applies as if its reference to section 806(a)(2) referred to section 1784 of title 10, and the held current text of 10 U.S.C. 1784(a)(2) carries the same preference authority. The order also cites 3 U.S.C. 301, which is held and in force. The Code prints the order as a note with no ending statement; the Federal Register disposition notes list no amendment or revocation.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: the text sets no term or condition, and the repeal-and-replacement of the statutory reference was handled by Pub. L. 104-106 section 568(d), which keeps the order in effect rather than ending it.","independent_command_check":"The empowerment of the Secretary of Defense and of the designated military department officials is one command; the preference authority itself is conferred by statute and is not a separate command of the order.","savings_check":"No ending event, so no savings question arises.","scope_check":"Single operative scope: the whole sole paragraph delegating the discretionary preference authority for nonappropriated fund positions to the Secretary of Defense and his designees."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order is a continuing delegation with no end; Congress in 1996 directed that it apply as if it referred to 10 U.S.C. 1784, and no later instrument ending it was found, so no residual exists beyond the operative clause.

AGENCY: Immigration and Naturalization

a c t i o n: Final rule.
SUMMARY: This rule adds Compania 
Panamena de Aviacion S.A. (COPA) to 
the list of carriers which have entered 
into agreements with the Service to 
guarantee the passage through the 
United States in immediate and 
continuous transit of aliens destined to 
foreign countries.
EFFECTIVE DATE: September 15,1986.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.  
Loretta J. Shogren, Director, Policy 
Directives and Instructions, Immigration  
and Naturalization Service, 4251  Street, 
NW., Washington, DC 20536. Telephone: 
(202) 633-3048.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The 
Commissioner of Immigration and 
Naturalization entered into an 
agreement with Compania Panamena de 
Aviacion S.A. (COPA), on September 15, 
1986, to guarantee passage through the 
United States in immediate and 
continuous transit of aliens destined to 
foreign countries.
The agreement provides for the 
waiver of certain documentary 
requirements and facilitates the air 
travel of passengers on international 
flights while passing through the United 
States.

notice of proposed rulemaking and 
delayed effective date is unnecessary 
because the amendment merely makes
an editorial change to the listing of 
transportation lines.

Commissioner of Immigration and 
Naturalization certifies that the rule will 
not have a significant impact on a 
substantial number of small entities.

public under 5 U.S.C. 552 and is not a 
rule within the definition of section 1(a) 
of E .0 .12291.

THE FLAG OF THE UNITED STATES
WHEREAS the State of Hawaii has 
this day been admitted into the Union; and
WHEREAS section 2 of title 4 of the 
United States Code provides as follows: 
“On the admission of a new State into 
the Union one star shall be added to the 
union of the flag; and such addition 
shall take effect on the fourth day of 
July then next succeeding such admis­sion.”; and
WHEREAS the Federal Property and 
Administrative Services Act of 1949 (63 
®iat. 377), as amended, authorizes the
President to prescribe policies and direc­
tives governing the procurement and 
utilization of property by executive agen­
cies; and
WHEREAS the interests of the Gov­
ernment require that orderly and reason­
able provision be made for various m at­
ters pertaining to the flag and that 
appropriate regulations governing the 
procurement and utilization of national 
flags and union jacks by executive agen­
cies be prescribed:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me as President of 
the United States and as Commander in 
Ciilef of the armed forces of the United 
States,' *\nd the Federal Property and 
Administrative Services Act of 1949, as 
amended, it is hereby ordered as follows:
P art I—D esign  of the F lag
S ection  1. The flag of the United 
States shall have thirteen horizontal 
stripes, alternate red and white, and a 
union consisting of white stars on a field 
of blue.
Sec. 2. The positions of the stars in 
the union of the flag and in the union 
jack shall be as indicated on the attach­
ment to this order, which is hereby made 
a part of this order.
Sec. 3. The dimensions of the consti­
tuent parts of the flag shall conform to 
the proportions set forth in the attach­
ment referred to in section 2 of this 
order.

prised within the Sand Island Military

ordered as follows:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The held text of section 2, which provides that the positions of the stars in the union of the flag and the union jack are as indicated on the attachment, which is made part of the order. It states no expiry or condition, no held later instrument revokes or amends it, and the Code prints the order as current and still defines the flag by reference to it, so the clause was operative on 2026-10-14.

current_predicate.legal_basis: The held U.S. Code (release point 119-121, edition through 2026-10-09) prints the full text of Executive Order 10834, titled Proportions and Sizes of Flags and Position of Stars, as a note under 4 U.S.C. 1 with no amendment or ending statement, and 4 U.S.C. 5 (added by Pub. L. 105-225, section 2(a), Aug. 12, 1998) defines the flag of the United States for the chapter according to sections 1 and 2 of title 4 and Executive Order 10834 issued pursuant thereto. Bounded eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and Federal Register disposition-note search (which lists only that the order revokes EO 10798) found no revocation or amendment.

WHEREAS the act of August 25, 1958 
(72 Stat. 850), authorizes the President of

that land comprising any portion or por­
tions of Sand Island Military Reservation 
and the Navy Harbor Entrance Control 
Post, Honolulu, Territory of Hawaii, in­
cluding submerged lands therein, not to 
exceed in the aggregate 202 acres, is no 
longer required or is not required for 
military purposes, to transfer to the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii, by Executive Order, all 
the right, title and interest of the United 
States in said land, together with the im­
provements thereon, and to grant non­
exclusive easements over other land com­
prised within the Sand Island Military 
Reservation and the Navy Harbor En­
trance Control Post in favor of the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii which he shall deem 
necessary for the proper enjoyment of 
the premises transferred; and 
WHEREAS the hereinafter-described 
land is not required for military pur­
poses;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by the above- 
mentioned act of August 25, 1958, it is 
ordered as follows:

THE FLAG OF THE UNITED STATES
WHEREAS the State of Hawaii has 
this day been admitted into the Union; and
WHEREAS section 2 of title 4 of the 
United States Code provides as follows: 
“On the admission of a new State into 
the Union one star shall be added to the 
union of the flag; and such addition 
shall take effect on the fourth day of 
July then next succeeding such admis­sion.”; and
WHEREAS the Federal Property and 
Administrative Services Act of 1949 (63 
®iat. 377), as amended, authorizes the
President to prescribe policies and direc­
tives governing the procurement and 
utilization of property by executive agen­
cies; and
WHEREAS the interests of the Gov­
ernment require that orderly and reason­
able provision be made for various m at­
ters pertaining to the flag and that 
appropriate regulations governing the 
procurement and utilization of national 
flags and union jacks by executive agen­
cies be prescribed:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me as President of 
the United States and as Commander in 
Ciilef of the armed forces of the United 
States,' *\nd the Federal Property and 
Administrative Services Act of 1949, as 
amended, it is hereby ordered as follows:
P art I—D esign  of the F lag
S ection  1. The flag of the United 
States shall have thirteen horizontal 
stripes, alternate red and white, and a 
union consisting of white stars on a field 
of blue.
Sec. 2. The positions of the stars in 
the union of the flag and in the union 
jack shall be as indicated on the attach­
ment to this order, which is hereby made 
a part of this order.
Sec. 3. The dimensions of the consti­
tuent parts of the flag shall conform to 
the proportions set forth in the attach­
ment referred to in section 2 of this 
order.

chased for the use of executive agencies :
(a) Shall conform to the provisions of

in respect of procurement for the De­
partment of Defense (including military 
colors) and the Administrator of Gen­
eral Services in respect of procurement 
for executive agencies other than the 
Department of Defense may, for cause 
which the Secretary or the Administra­
tor, as the case may be, deems sufficient, 
make necessary minor adjustments in 
one or more of the dimensions or pro­
portionate dimensions prescribed by this 
order, or authorize proportions or sizes 
other than those prescribed by section 3 
or section 21 of this order.
(b) So far as practicable, (1) the ac­
tions of the Secretary of Defense under 
the provisions of section 24(a) of this 
order, as they relate to the various or­
ganizational elements of the Department 
of Defense, shall be coordinated, and (2) 
the Secretary and the Administrator 
shall mutually coordinate their actions 
under that section.
Sec. 25. Subject to such limited ex­
ceptions as the Secretary of Defense in 
respect of the Department of Defense, 
and the Administrator of General Serv­
ices in respect of executive agencies 
other than the Department of Defense, 
may approve, all national flags and 
union jacks now in the possession of exe­
cutive agencies, or hereafter acquired
by executive agencies under contracts 
awarded prior to the date of this order, 
including those so possessed or so ac­
quired by the General Services Adminis­
tration for distribution to other agencies, 
shall be utilized until unserviceable.
P art III— General P rovisions
S ec. 31. The flag prescribed by Execu­
tive Order No. 10798 of January 3, 1959, 
shall be the official flag of the United 
States until July 4,1960, and on that date 
the flag prescribed by Part I of this order 
shall become the official flag of the 
United States; but this section shall 
neither "derogate from section 24 or sec­
tion 25 of this order nor preclude the 
procurement, for executive agencies, of 
flags provided for by or pursuant to this 
order at any time after the date of this 
order.

“executive agencies” means the execu­
tive departments and independent es­
tablishments in the executive branch of 
the Government, including wholly- 
owijed Government corporations.

January 3, 1959, is hereby revoked.

Executive Order 10833
TRANSFERRING TITLE TO CERTAIN  
LANDS AT SAND ISLAND, TERRI­
TORY OF HAWAII, TO THE TERRI­
TORY OF HAWAII
WHEREAS the act of August 25, 1958 
(72 Stat. 850), authorizes the President of 
the United States, when he determines 
that land comprising any portion or por­
tions of Sand Island Military Reservation 
and the Navy Harbor Entrance Control 
Post, Honolulu, Territory of Hawaii, in­
cluding submerged lands therein, not to 
exceed in the aggregate 202 acres, is no 
longer required or is not required for 
military purposes, to transfer to the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii, by Executive Order, all 
the right, title and interest of the United 
States in said land, together with the im­
provements thereon, and to grant non­
exclusive easements over other land com­
prised within the Sand Island Military 
Reservation and the Navy Harbor En­
trance Control Post in favor of the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii which he shall deem 
necessary for the proper enjoyment of 
the premises transferred; and 
WHEREAS the hereinafter-described 
land is not required for military pur­
poses;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by the above- 
mentioned act of August 25, 1958, it is 
ordered as follows:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The held text of section 25, which provides that flags and union jacks in the possession of executive agencies, or acquired under contracts awarded before the order, are used until unserviceable, subject to approved exceptions. It states no expiry or condition, no held later instrument revokes or amends it, and the Code prints the order as current and still defines the flag by reference to it, so the clause was operative on 2026-10-14.

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 10834
THE FLAG OF THE UNITED STATES
WHEREAS the State of Hawaii has 
this day been admitted into the Union; and
WHEREAS section 2 of title 4 of the 
United States Code provides as follows: 
“On the admission of a new State into 
the Union one star shall be added to the 
union of the flag; and such addition 
shall take effect on the fourth day of 
July then next succeeding such admis­sion.”; and
WHEREAS the Federal Property and 
Administrative Services Act of 1949 (63 
®iat. 377), as amended, authorizes the
President to prescribe policies and direc­
tives governing the procurement and 
utilization of property by executive agen­
cies; and
WHEREAS the interests of the Gov­
ernment require that orderly and reason­
able provision be made for various m at­
ters pertaining to the flag and that 
appropriate regulations governing the 
procurement and utilization of national 
flags and union jacks by executive agen­
cies be prescribed:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me as President of 
the United States and as Commander in 
Ciilef of the armed forces of the United 
States,' *\nd the Federal Property and 
Administrative Services Act of 1949, as 
amended, it is hereby ordered as follows:
P art I—D esign  of the F lag
S ection  1. The flag of the United 
States shall have thirteen horizontal 
stripes, alternate red and white, and a 
union consisting of white stars on a field 
of blue.
Sec. 2. The positions of the stars in 
the union of the flag and in the union 
jack shall be as indicated on the attach­
ment to this order, which is hereby made 
a part of this order.
Sec. 3. The dimensions of the consti­
tuent parts of the flag shall conform to 
the proportions set forth in the attach­
ment referred to in section 2 of this 
order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The held text of section 31, which makes the flag prescribed by EO 10798 the official flag until July 4, 1960 and makes the flag prescribed by Part I the official flag on that date. By its own terms the transition was complete on July 4, 1960, when the Part I flag became the official flag; the section says until July 4, 1960, so the exclusive reading is that the period of the earlier flag ended as that day began and the inclusive reading is that it ran through that day, and the order itself places the changeover on that date, which is recorded as the end. Clause exhausted by its own terms; the continuing predicate for the order comes from the other scopes.

research_rationale:
EO 10834 (Eisenhower, signed 1959-08-21, 24 FR 6865, published 1959-08-25) was issued on the admission of Hawaii and prescribes the design of the flag with fifty stars (Part I: sections 1 to 3, with the position of stars and the proportions set out in an attachment made part of the order), the sizes of flags authorized for executive agencies and rules for their procurement (Part II: sections 21 to 25) and general provisions (Part III: section 31 making the flag of EO 10798 official until July 4, 1960 and the Part I flag official on that date, section 32 defining executive agencies, and section 33 revoking EO 10798). The dossier inventory omitted section 1, ran section 3 across about 7,900 characters of Federal Register front matter, split the section 21 size table into row fragments and omitted sections 22 to 24 and 31 to 32 as separate scopes, so the inventory is corrected with overrides to eleven scopes covering every section of the held text. Sections 31 and 33 are spent by their own terms: section 33 revoked EO 10798 on signing, and section 31 provided for the changeover on July 4, 1960 (the order states no other effective date, and 4 U.S.C. 2, recited in the order, fixes July 4 as the effective date of an added star). The remaining sections have no term or condition. The held Code prints the whole order as a current note, with no amendment, under 4 U.S.C. 1, and 4 U.S.C. 5 still defines the flag by reference to it. ernment require that orderly and reason­

research_rationale:
EO 12626 (Reagan, signed 1988-02-25, 53 FR 6114, published 1988-02-29) designates the Secretary of Defense as National Defense Stockpile Manager and delegates to him the functions vested in the President by the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act except those under sections 7, 8 and 13 of the Act (section 8(a) functions go to the Secretary of the Interior and section 8(b) functions to the Secretary of Agriculture) (section 1); delegates the functions under section 4(h) of the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act (section 2) and under section 204(f) of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (section 3) to the Secretary of Defense; and authorizes redelegation with consultation (section 4). The Federal Register text in the dossier inventory starts at section 1, so the authority recital (Stock Piling Act, section 3203 of Pub. L. 100-180 and 3 U.S.C. 301) is read as context. The held Code notes to 50 U.S.C. 98 print the full order as a current note and show no ending or amendment; EO 14051 of October 31, 2021, printed there, designates the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment under 50 U.S.C. 98f, the section 7 function that section 1 of EO 12626 excludes, and says nothing that revokes or amends EO 12626. The authority statutes are in force: the Stock Piling Act (50 U.S.C. 98 et seq.) and 3 U.S.C. 301 are held; section 4(h) of the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act is held in the 2024 U.S. Code edition of 15 U.S.C. 714b, which carries a note that the subsection is delegated to the Secretary of Defense by section 2 of this order; the text of former 40 U.S.C. 485(f), now 40 U.S.C. 574(d) per the Code note, is not held (see the section 3 clause). A search of the held corpus for the order number finds only its own text, the 1989 codification and Code notes.
